title: Secrets catalog
description: The secrets catalog, as defined in The Software Field Guide, issue #108: the platform's word for the secrets that exist. Each cataloged secret names its kind (which decides how a leak ages and how rotation is done), the one scope it grants (never a wildcard), its rotation clock (the day it last rotated and the age that clock must not reach), and the identities admitted as its consumers — permission is granted here, never assumed by a manifest. The catalog is honest about what it models: every secret declared with a kind, a scope, a live rotation clock, and named consumers — not that rotation actually happened; that answer lives in the platform's secret store and its tooling, not in policy. This schema mirrors the shape rules of the Rego validator (policies/identity); the validator additionally enforces the semantic rules a JSON schema cannot — reviewedOn and rotatedOn real calendar dates not in the future, no reviewed catalog older than 365 days, the modeled kinds only, no glob-shaped or wildcard scopes, no duplicate secrets or consumers, maxAgeDays a positive number, and the joins judged at the gate against the identity manifest.

version.description: Version of the catalog. An unversioned catalog is a catalog nobody can pin a rotation against.

reviewedOn.description: Date the catalog was last reviewed, YYYY-MM-DD. The validator flags reviews older than 365 days and dates in the future.

owner.description: The team that owns the catalog and answers for the secrets it declares. A catalog with an owner and a review cadence is the discipline.

secrets.description: The secrets the platform holds, one row per secret. One secret, one row: a credential declared twice is a credential nobody can vouch for once.

name.description: The secret's name. The manifest references secrets by this name, and the gate joins on it — an unnamed secret is a grant nobody can scope.

kind.description: The secret's kind. How a credential authenticates decides how it must be rotated. The validator models api-key, service-token, signing-key, and certificate, and refuses a kind it never agreed to.

scope.description: The one scope the secret grants. The catalog exists to name grants, not to grant everything — a scope that means everything is a breach nobody can bound, and the validator refuses wildcards and glob shapes.

rotatedOn.description: The day the secret last rotated, YYYY-MM-DD. A secret with no rotation clock is a credential the platform holds forever; the validator flags dates that are not real or in the future, and the gate refuses a clock that ran out.

maxAgeDays.description: The age the secret's rotation may reach, in days. A clock with nothing to measure against never rings — a zero-day clock is a rotation schedule nobody can keep.

consumers.description: The identities admitted to consume the secret, by name. Permission is granted by the catalog, never assumed by the manifest — a consumer nobody can name is permission nobody can revoke. The list may be empty: a deliberately reserved secret is availability, not a drift.

items.description: An admitted consumer's identity name, exactly as the manifest declares it. One identity, one entry.
